content: 1. In a 2012 study conducted in India, involving a lower-middle-income population, 96 individuals were recruited from a hospital setting. Of these, 79% were men. The diagnosis of herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) was based on clinical evaluation, Tzanck smear, and IgM serology. The study reported 33 true positives, 38 false negatives, 25 false positives, and 302 true negatives. 2. Between 1990 and 1992, a study in Rwanda, a low-income country, included 395 participants recruited from general practice clinics, with 63% being men. Diagnosis of genital ulcer disease was based on patient history and physical examination. Cytopathic effects on Vero cells were used as the diagnostic method, yielding 485 true positives, 430 false negatives, 302 false positives, and 219 true negatives. 3. Another study in Rwanda during the same period (1990–1992) used a combination of clinical history, physical examination, syphilis serology, or dark-field microscopy to diagnose syphilis in individuals with genital ulcer disease. The diagnostic method identified 107 true positives, 39 false negatives, 276 false positives, and 6 true negatives. 4. A study conducted in the United States between 1990 and 1992, involving 220 men from a sexual health clinic, used clinical diagnosis and culture as the diagnostic method. The results showed 20 true positives, 37 false negatives, 10 false positives, and 153 true negatives. 5. In India, during 2015–2016, a study involving 96 participants (75% men) from a sexual health clinic used clinical diagnosis, Tzanck smear, and HSV-2 IgM serology. The study reported 33 true positives, 36 false negatives, 25 false positives, and 302 true negatives. 6. A study in Lesotho (1993–1994) recruited 92 participants from a sexual health clinic. Clinical diagnosis was supported by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (M-PCR). The study reported 7 true positives, 10 false negatives, 1 false positive, and 74 true negatives. 7. Another study in Lesotho during the same period (1993–1994) used M-PCR for diagnosis and reported 5 true positives, 19 false negatives, 3 false positives, and 65 true negatives. 8. In India (2008–2009), a study involving 181 men from a sexual health clinic used M-PCR for diagnosis. The results showed 59 true positives, 31 false negatives, 37 false positives, and 54 true negatives. 9. A study in the Dominican Republic (1995–1996) recruited 81 men from general practice clinics. Using M-PCR, the study identified 19 true positives, 16 false negatives, 10 false positives, and 36 true negatives. 10. In China (1998–1999), a study involving 96 participants (52% men) from a sexual health clinic used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported 25 true positives, 8 false negatives, 36 false positives, and 27 true negatives. 11. Another study in China (2000–2001) recruited 227 participants (90% men) from a sexual health clinic. Diagnosis was based on symptoms, examination, and risk factors, using M-PCR, dark-field microscopy, and serological tests. The study reported 49 true positives, 22 false negatives, 78 false positives, and 78 true negatives. 12. In Kenya (1980), a study involving 70 men from a special treatment clinic used clinical diagnosis and culture. The results showed 33 true positives, 1 false negative, and 63 true negatives. 13. A study in South Africa (unclear year) recruited 210 men from a hospital setting. Diagnosis was based on clinical evaluation and culture, yielding 52 true positives, 21 false negatives, 18 false positives, and 182 true negatives. 14. In Madagascar (1997), a study involving 196 participants (71% men) from a sexual health clinic used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported 52 true positives, 4 false negatives, 112 false positives, and 28 true negatives. 15. A study in Jamaica (1996) recruited 304 men from a sexual health clinic. Using M-PCR, the study identified 21 true positives, 10 false negatives, 24 false positives, and 249 true negatives. 16. In Thailand (1995–1996), a study involving 38 female sex workers from a sexual health clinic used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported no true positives, 1 false negative, 1 false positive, and 36 true negatives. 17. In India (2011–2012), a study involving 96 participants (79% men) from a hospital setting used clinical diagnosis and Gram stain. The study reported 21 true positives, 1 false negative, and 92 true negatives. 18. A study in Rwanda (1990–1992) involving 395 participants (63% men) used clinical history, examination, and culture for diagnosis. The study reported 115 true positives, no false negatives, 272 false positives, and 8 true negatives. 19. Another study in Rwanda during the same period used clinical history, examination, syphilis serology, or dark-field microscopy for diagnosis. The study reported 83 true positives, 32 false negatives, 188 false positives, and 92 true negatives. 20. In Kenya (1990–1991), a study involving 172 participants (47% men) from primary care settings used clinical diagnosis and RPR for syphilis detection. The study reported 6 true positives, 18 false negatives, 19 false positives, and 129 true negatives. 21. In India (2008–2009), a study involving 181 men from a sexual health clinic used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported 26 true positives, 18 false negatives, 72 false positives, and 78 true negatives. 22. In the Dominican Republic (1995–1996), a study involving 81 men from general practice clinics used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported 22 true positives, 11 false negatives, and 66 true negatives. 23. In Peru (1995–1996), a study involving 63 men from general practice clinics used M-PCR for diagnosis. The study reported no true positives, 3 false negatives, 21 false positives, and 39 true negatives. 24. In Kenya (1980), a study involving 70 men from a special treatment clinic used clinical diagnosis and culture. The study reported 42 true positives, 6 false negatives, and 68 true negatives. 25. In South Africa (unclear year), a study involving 210 men from a hospital setting used clinical diagnosis and culture. The study reported 117 true positives, 30 false negatives, 14 false positives, and 49 true negatives.
